test_name: BatchData corrected Search and Lookup contract capability probe

contracts_tested.lookup_request_shape: requests[].address as structured street/city/state/zip plus requestId

request_exposure.billing_note: take:0 may carry a minimum record charge; failed entitlement requests and multi-dataset pricing must be confirmed in the provider dashboard

corrected_lookup_results.interpretation: The corrected Lookup endpoint and structured request work with basic, but the token cannot request the rich datasets needed for enrichment.

qualified_basic_mapper_evidence_suppleme.route_date_gate_interpretation: The pure selectRecentSaleEvidence function returned no date for all three records. Therefore the pre-provenance mapper's missing-sale-date gate would reject all three, even though Search was qualified by the provider-side Intel date predicate. Production now preserves exact job-scoped predicate evidence; this statement covers returned date fields only.

qualified_seattle_intel_cursor_round_tri.criteria: Same 14-day Intel, R2, minimum $100k estimated value, and not Active/Pending Seattle polygon criteria on both calls
qualified_seattle_intel_cursor_round_tri.options_page_2: identical plus pageCursor set to the verbatim opaque nextPageCursor from page 1
qualified_seattle_intel_cursor_round_tri.interpretation: Cursor initialization worked, but one verbatim round-trip failed. Cursor pagination is not production-reliable for this token without a bounded offset fallback. A single HTTP 500 does not distinguish a persistent account contract failure from a transient provider failure.

findings: All provider-side R2, valuation-floor, and listing-exclusion count requests were accepted with HTTP 200 using options.datasets=[basic].
No yesterday-only candidates were reported by Intel or Sale in any of the four polygons.
Intel produced six more fourteen-day candidates than Sale in Seattle and tied Sale in the other three polygons; count data cannot prove whether Sale is a subset.
In Seattle, R2 was the sole observed count-reducing gate; the $100k floor and Active/Pending exclusion did not remove additional candidates in this sample.
Corrected basic Lookup succeeded and matched the Search identity in all three samples.
Rich Lookup enrichment is blocked by dataset entitlement, not disproven by endpoint behavior.

Qualified basic Search returned complete addresses and coordinate pairs in three of three records, but none of the mapper's accepted returned-date paths; selectRecentSaleEvidence returned none for all three, so the pre-provenance strict date gate would reject all three.

Cursor page 1 returned HTTP 200, one of 11 candidates, and nextPageCursor; the identical page-2 request with that opaque cursor returned HTTP 500 and no record, so cursor pagination needs a bounded offset fallback.
limitations: This is a provider capability and relative-count test, not a penetration measurement against recorder or MLS ground truth.
Count equality does not prove record-set equality; maximum recall requires separately paginating and de-duplicating Intel and Sale results.
Provider acceptance of a filter is not an independent proof that every match is classified correctly.
Only three property identities and three supplemental mapper-evidence records were checked, and no PII or raw payload was retained.
The rich response shape could not be observed with this token because all requested rich datasets are disabled.
The cursor result is one no-retry round-trip; the HTTP 500 may be persistent or transient, so it proves fallback necessity rather than permanent cursor impossibility.
